zero_omission_notes.summary: Light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation of light). Materials are transparent (allow light fully), translucent (allow light partially), or opaque (block light completely). Shadows are dark regions formed on a screen when opaque objects obstruct light paths. Pinhole cameras demonstrate rectilinear propagation by forming real, inverted images. Reflection of light occurs when light hits smooth polished surfaces (plane mirrors), following the Law of Reflection: Angle of Incidence equals Angle of Reflection (i = r). Plane mirror images are virtual, erect, same size as object, and laterally inverted.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Viewing a candle flame through a straight pipe shows light; bending the pipe blocks light, proving straight-line propagation. Law of Reflection: Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie on the same plane; Angle i = Angle r. Lateral inversion causes left-right reversal.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Ambulance Lettering
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Emergency vehicles have 'AMBULANCE' printed in laterally inverted lettering so drivers ahead reading their rearview mirrors see the word correctly.

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: To construct a card pinhole camera and observe real inverted image formation.
procedure_or_steps: Make a small pinhole at the center of the outer box's front face.
Cut a square window on the inner box face and paste tracing paper over it.
Slide inner box inside outer box and point pinhole face toward a bright sunny tree or building.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: An inverted, colorful, smaller image of the outdoor object appears on the translucent tracing paper screen.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Light rays from top and bottom of object cross straight through the tiny pinhole, proving rectilinear propagation.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: 1. Angle of Incidence (i) = Angle of Reflection (r). 2. Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane.
The reversal of left and right orientation in an image formed by a plane mirror.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Raising right hand appears as left hand in mirror.

textbook_exercises.question: List three mandatory requirements for shadow formation.
textbook_exercises.answer: 1. A source of light. 2. An opaque or translucent object to block light. 3. A screen or background surface behind the object where shadow falls.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: The image formed by a pinhole camera is always:
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: Light rays traveling in straight lines cross through the pinhole, projecting a real inverted image on the screen.

short_answer_questions.question: Differentiate between a shadow and a mirror image.
short_answer_questions.answer: Shadow: Formed by light obstruction; dark region showing only object outline without color or detail. Mirror Image: Formed by light reflection; shows complete color, shape, and internal details of object.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: If a light ray strikes a plane mirror surface at an angle of 35 degrees with the mirror surface, what is the angle of reflection?
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: Angle with mirror = 35 deg. Normal is at 90 deg. Angle of Incidence (i) = 90 - 35 = 55 deg. By Law of Reflection (i = r), Angle of Reflection (r) = 55 degrees.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: State the Laws of Reflection, draw a labeled ray diagram, and list four characteristics of images formed by plane mirrors.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: Laws: 1. Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection (i = r). 2. Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie on the same plane. Image Characteristics: 1. Virtual (cannot be caught on screen). 2. Erect (upright). 3. Same size as object. 4. Laterally inverted (left-right reversed). Image distance behind mirror equals object distance in front.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: A student constructs a periscope using a long cardboard tube and two plane mirrors.

qa.question: At what angle must the two plane mirrors be fixed inside the periscope tube?
qa.answer: The two plane mirrors must be fixed parallel to each other at an angle of 45 degrees relative to the length of the tube, allowing double reflection to view objects above line of sight.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Measuring angle of incidence from the mirror surface rather than from the normal.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Angle of incidence is ALWAYS measured between the incident light ray and the normal (perpendicular 90-degree line).
